technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Cloud Data Flow's existing REST and Shell infrastructure to add module upload and registry management features.
Replace the hard-coded ModuleRegistryPopulator with a dynamic ModuleRegistry service that supports runtime registration and local filesystem persistence of uploaded module artifacts.
For dynamic reflection, uploaded modules will be registered in-memory immediately and persisted to a configurable directory; no cluster-wide sync in this increment.
Module upload will accept packaged module JARs via multipart HTTP requests; shell commands will wrap these REST calls.

Migrated XD modules will be adapted to the Spring Cloud Stream Source binding model (@EnableBinding(Source.class)) and placed as new submodules in the target repos (s-c-s-m for jms/mail/mongo, s-c-s for mqtt/reactor-ip/stdout).
Reuse existing Spring XD module logic as much as possible; only adapt packaging, configuration, and binder APIs.
assumptions: A single developer with existing knowledge of Spring Cloud Data Flow and Spring XD performs all work; effort is expressed in person-workdays (8-hour days).
Target repositories are already set up with build tooling (Maven/Gradle); only source code and build configs for new modules are added.
The module registry persistence uses local filesystem; multi-node deployment and high availability are out of scope.
Integration testing of migrated modules assumes a local message broker (e.g., RabbitMQ) is available; if not, tests are written but may be skipped.
Uploaded custom modules are assumed to be compliant with the Spring Cloud Data Flow module format; validation is minimal.
The specification's mention of 'stdout' as a source is taken literally; the module will be adapted as a source (e.g., reading from stdin or generating heartbeat messages) to satisfy the requirement.
Java version required by target repos is already met (assumed Java 8/11); no Java 17 migration is performed unless forced by the repo.
